I decided each reader separately, added a test for each, and committed. Eight tests in `src/quack/spawns_runner_test.go` fail, but they fail the same way without my change. I didn't investigate why. I also didn't confirm whether `./RUNME.sh check` passes. It ran 154s against its 120s budget, and I only grepped its output for failures. `go test ./src/pull` passes, and so do the new and neighbouring Vale tests.

- **`voiceRunsValeOver`** (`src/quack/voice_verb.go`): a run a signal ends now answers a fault, so the code -2 doesn't slip through as output with no fault. A killed Vale leaves partial output, so I treated it as a failure. The fault reads `vale: a signal ended the run: <stderr>`. The new test is `TestVoiceRunsValeAnswersAFaultForAValeASignalEnds`.
- **`ShellOver`** (`src/pull/door.go`): I left the behaviour alone, so a signalled line answers its output and exit -2 with no fault. The command runner records that exit and checks it against the field's `expects`, so a signalled line fails there instead of aborting the evidence run. I only added a doc comment saying so. The new test is `TestTheShellReadsALineASignalEndsAsItsExitWithNoFault`.

I didn't touch the size or callers-line limits you mentioned.

The commit is `fb3feec`.
